clue.text: Bird, and a second fabulous creature

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, especially a rooster
a trice is an instant, a second

explanation.surface: Someone sights a bird and then a second mythical beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockatrice is a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg, a beast of fable.

clue.text: Brandy up? Stuff!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape pressings

explanation.surface: Someone urging another to drink up the brandy and stuff themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: To cram is to stuff full, used as an exclamatory command.

clue.text: How one may pay — with a lot of notes in the end

definitions.text: a lot of notes in the end

parts.note: COD, cash on delivery, is a way of paying

explanation.surface: Explaining how to pay with lots of banknotes eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is a closing passage of music, many notes at a piece's end.

clue.text: Ira cut out nothing in Latin speech

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of Ira cut are disordered
in places the round letter for nothing inside the word Latin

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Ira cuts nothing from a speech in Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: Articulation is the clear utterance of words, the act of speaking.

clue.text: Radical entertains Socialist leader in place of retirement

indicators.note: entertains means hosts, holding a guest inside

parts.note: a radical in maths or language is a root

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An extremist hosts a left-wing chief at a retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is where birds settle for the night, a place to retire to sleep.

clue.text: Talked quickly from notes about mad Dodgsonian

indicators.note: about means going round, so the notes surround the other piece

parts.note: C, E and D are musical notes
the Mad Hatter is a character created by Charles Dodgson (Lewis Carroll)

explanation.surface: Someone spoke fast from notes about a crazy Carroll character.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodgson was the real name of Lewis Carroll, author of Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter is to talk rapidly and idly.

clue.text: Metal to act as conductor

explanation.surface: A metal that can serve as an electrical conductor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead is a heavy grey metal; to lead is to conduct or guide, as a conductor leads an orchestra.

clue.text: Faded look ruined Titian oleo

indicators.note: ruined indicates the letters of the painter and oleo are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A damaged oil painting by Titian looks faded.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiolation is pallor from lack of light, a faded, washed-out appearance.

clue.text: Lady in trouble — about to drop off — PT needed

indicators.note: about means around, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
trouble, taken as stirring up, shows the letters of Lady in are disturbed

parts.note: to doze is to drop off to sleep

explanation.surface: A lady in difficulty, about to fall asleep, needs exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lady in trouble' looks like a damsel in distress, but 'in' is fodder and 'trouble' alone stirs the letters; PT is physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: The daily dozen are a set of morning physical exercises, a routine of physical training.

clue.text: More Italian — odd, very odd

indicators.note: something very odd is strange or bizarre, so these letters are put into a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone finds yet another Italian quite peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'odd' is fodder; the second, in 'very odd', is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional means extra, so it can stand for more, as in 'more help'.

clue.text: Shouldn't Puccini's girl have worn gloves?

definitions.text: Shouldn't Puccini's girl have worn gloves?

parts.words: Shouldn't Puccini's girl have worn gloves?
parts.note: in La Boheme the poet sings to the heroine that her tiny hand is frozen, so the question names the opera's seamstress

explanation.surface: A wry question about a cold-handed opera heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: The aria 'Che gelida manina' (Your tiny hand is frozen) is sung to her in Act 1 of La Boheme.
explanation.definitionFit: The seamstress heroine of Puccini's La Boheme, whose cold hand Rodolfo warms.

clue.text: Place for cake — one with wine about is divine

parts.note: Eccles, a town near Manchester, gives its name to the Eccles cake, a currant pastry
I is the Roman numeral one
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A town for pastries, where someone with wine is in heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: A divine is a cleric or theologian, a churchman.

clue.text: City still has a friend in raptures

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
static means still, not moving
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone in the City is delighted to have a friend there still.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in raptures is to act with intense delight, an adverbial phrase matching the adverb.

clue.text: Guarantees to organize a hundred nurses, as at first

indicators.note: to organize means to arrange, so the pieces are put into a new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hospital promise to manage a hundred nurses as before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' is surface padding: the anagram pool is A, C, NURSES and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurances are promises or pledges, the same as guarantees.

clue.text: In stormy weather opposed to northern meat dishes

indicators.note: In puts the following pieces inside the word for stormy weather

parts.note: gales are stormy winds
anti means against, opposed to

explanation.surface: In bad weather someone objects to northern meat dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Galantines are cold dishes of boned meat set in aspic.

clue.text: "To suckle fools and chronicle " said Iago

definitions.text: "To suckle fools and chronicle " said Iago

parts.words: "To suckle fools and chronicle " said Iago
parts.note: the line from Othello ends with a phrase for trivial matters, which the solver supplies

explanation.surface: A quotation from Othello with its last two words missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Iago in Othello, Act 2, says a worthy woman is fit only to suckle fools and chronicle trivia.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means trivial things, literally weak beer.

clue.text: 6 with hesitation followed by our readers?

definitions.text: 6 with hesitation followed by our readers?

parts.words: 6 with hesitation followed by our readers?
parts.note: the metal answer at 6 across plus the hesitation er gives a newspaper's opinion column, which readers follow

explanation.surface: A newspaper's lead piece followed by its readership.
explanation.walkthrough: In British papers the leader is the editorial column.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's leading article is its opinion column, which its readers follow.

clue.text: Many a Turk unmanned by this game

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so a large number

indicators.note: being unmanned means losing the word for a man, which is dropped

parts.note: an Ottoman is a Turk of the old empire

explanation.surface: A game that leaves many a Turkish player unnerved.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a game of chance played with numbered cards, like bingo.

clue.text: Girl takes part that's not suitable

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl takes on an acting part that doesn't suit her.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt means inappropriate, an old synonym of unfit.

clue.text: Din changed one's attitude put one off

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of the word din are rearranged

parts.note: one's is read as I (one) plus 's, giving IS
a pose is a bodily attitude

explanation.surface: The noise altered someone's stance and put them off.
explanation.definitionFit: To indispose is to make someone unwilling or averse, to put them off.

clue.text: Huge claim — or not, as amended

indicators.note: amended suggests the words are corrected and so rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge claim, which may or may not be true once corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical figures are enormous, vast like the distances in space.

clue.text: Girl points in anger

indicators.note: in places the compass points inside the word for anger

parts.note: ire is anger
E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: A girl makes sharp remarks in a temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is a girl's name.

clue.text: Speed negative, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for negative is matched by sound with the answer

parts.note: not is a negative word

explanation.surface: A rumour that speed is a bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a unit of speed at sea, one nautical mile per hour.

clue.text: Man Bites Dog (vide Dana)

parts.note: Charles Dana of the New York Sun is credited with saying a dog biting a man is no story, but a man biting a dog is worth printing

explanation.surface: A headline with a citation to a newspaper editor.
explanation.walkthrough: Vide is Latin for see, used to cite a source.
explanation.definitionFit: The reversal of the ordinary is what makes a story worth reporting in the papers.

clue.text: Inclination without ability?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a leaning implies lack of talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is a slope or tilt; read as can't, it means unable to.

clue.text: Dabbler in art, wrongly titled, gets payment in advance

indicators.note: wrongly signals that the letters of the word titled are put out of order

parts.note: an ante is a stake paid in advance in poker

explanation.surface: An art amateur with a mistaken title is paid up front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is an amateur who dabbles, especially in the arts.

clue.text: Frame made of southern wood

parts.note: ash is a timber tree

explanation.surface: A frame built from wood out of the south.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass of a window.

clue.text: Change delicacies, causing wrangles

parts.note: to alter is to change
cates is an old word for dainty foods

explanation.surface: Swapping fancy dishes leads to quarrels.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to quarrel heatedly, so it altercates means it wrangles.
